title: 2026 U.S. House election for California's 46th Congressional District
description: The 2026 general election for California's 46th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat Lou Correa against Republican David Pan. The district covers central Orange County, including Anaheim, Santa Ana, Fullerton, Orange, Placentia, and Stanton, where registered Democrats hold a nearly 2-to-1 advantage over Republicans. Correa, a veteran Orange County politician first elected to Congress in 2016, is seeking a sixth term. Pan, a UC Irvine professor and former management consultant, previously challenged Correa in 2024 and advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary as the second-place finisher. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D,' reflecting the district's strong Democratic lean.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for this specific general election matchup. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D' based on district fundamentals.

candidates.name: Lou Correa
candidates.summary: Lou Correa is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 46th Congressional District, first elected in 2016. Born in Los Angeles to working-class Mexican immigrant parents, he earned a BA in Economics from CSU Fullerton and a JD and MBA from UCLA. He previously served in the California State Assembly, on the Orange County Board of Supervisors, and in the California State Senate. In Congress, he serves on the House Judiciary and Homeland Security Committees and is the Ranking Member of the Border Security Subcommittee, focusing on middle-class opportunity, immigration, and infrastructure.

candidates.name: David Pan
candidates.summary: David Tse-Chien Pan is a professor of German at the University of California, Irvine and the Republican nominee for California's 46th Congressional District. Born in 1963, he earned a BA from Stanford University and a PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Washington University (St. Louis), Stanford, and Penn State, and worked as a management consultant at McKinsey & Company. He previously served on the U.S. Commission on Unalienable Rights and ran unsuccessfully for this seat in 2024. His campaign focuses on public safety, school choice, and welfare reform.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific general election polling exists for this matchup, so the forecast relies entirely on structural district fundamentals. Democrats hold a nearly 2-to-1 voter registration advantage in CA-46. Incumbent Democrat Lou Correa has held the seat since 2016 and is seeking a sixth term; he defeated the same Republican challenger, David Pan, by roughly a 68%-32% margin in 2024. Pan again advanced through the 2026 top-two primary as the second-place finisher. Cook Political Report rates the race 'Solid D,' consistent with the district's strong Democratic lean. The absence of direct matchup polling reduces confidence from high to medium, but the fundamentals overwhelmingly favor Correa.
